title: Finite locally projective coefficient modules are dualizable
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring, S any scheme, and L a module over the pulled-back ring Λ_S on the small pro-etale site of S. Suppose that for every site object V there is a covering sieve such that on each domain W the restriction of L is a retract of Λ_W^r for some finite r, in the sense of [def-pur-condensed-finite-locally-projective]. Then L is dualizable for the relative tensor product: there exists a module D and evaluation L tensor D → Λ_S and coevaluation Λ_S → D tensor L satisfying both triangular identities.

source.place: Proof step 3, finite projective evaluation calculation

proof.text: For a finite free module, prove dualizability by induction on the number of factors: the empty product is zero and dualizable; the successor product is isomorphic to the biproduct of the unit and the previous product. Dualizability passes to biproducts and retracts. Thus every local splitting in [def-pur-condensed-finite-locally-projective] makes the restricted module dualizable. These are the proved private finite-power and retract lemmas in the Lean module.

For t = ihomUnitTensorToIhom L L, [lem-proetale-pullback-internal-hom] and the monoidal comparison identify its pullback to each covering domain with the same map for the restricted module. Local dualizability from step 1 makes the latter invertible. This uses Functor.Monoidal.isIso_map_ihomUnitTensorToIhom_of_ihomComparison, whose hypotheses are precisely the monoidality and internal-Hom comparison supplied here.

Forget module structures. Identify inverse image to a covering domain with localization restriction. Evaluate the pulled-back map at the identity object of that domain to obtain invertibility at that object of the original site. Sheaf.isIso_of_isIso_app_of_mem now descends invertibility along the covering sieves. The module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. Finally MonoidalClosed.exactPairingOfIsIso constructs the internal-dual exact pairing from invertibility of t; symmetry gives a right dual. All these descent and pairing steps are written out in Lean.
